summary.name: Habitat
summary.one_liner: A habit tracker that study groups share, so nobody quits alone.
summary.status: MVP scoped and prototype schema built; pricing undecided. Upfront costs beyond store fees are still guesses.
summary.problem: Students start habit apps and quit within two weeks, mostly because they are doing it alone.
summary.solution: Small study groups share habits and check in together in one feed; streaks are kept as a group, not ranked against each other.
summary.audience: University students in study groups of 3 to 8, starting with one campus.
summary.why_now: Universities are investing in student-success programmes, and group study is already a habit students have.

journey.title: First concept
journey.summary: Started as a personal habit tracker for students, with streaks, full offline sync and native apps on Firebase. The first estimate was 10 weeks.

changes.text: Offline sync added for patchy campus wifi

journey.title: Interviews and the group pivot
journey.summary: Twelve interviews showed people quit because they track alone. Habits became shared within study groups, and the MVP was cut to 6 weeks.

changes.text: Habits are shared by a study group
The personal tracker was replaced by the group version
Offline sync dropped: doubles build time, 2 of 12 asked
React Native with Expo instead of two native apps

journey.title: Prototype and stack change
journey.summary: Modelling groups showed Firestore was a poor fit, so the backend moved to Supabase. A small part of offline came back as a read-only cache.

changes.text: Firebase retired: per-group rules were awkward
Read-only offline cache, about a week of work

journey.title: Business model research
journey.summary: Compared freemium with a campus licence and scanned competitors. Pricing is still open and depends on a conversation with a student-success office.

changes.text: Pricing: freemium or campus licence, undecided

journey.title: Launch planning
journey.summary: Set a one-campus launch, a four-phase plan, costs, risks and the team needed.

features.intro: Four things make the MVP. Everything else was deliberately deferred or cut; select a card to see why.

validation.verdict: The core insight (people quit when they track alone) has moderate support from 12 interviews. Nobody has paid yet, and one competitor already offers groups.

evidence.claim: 7 of 9 interviewees who had used habit apps quit within 2 weeks, mostly because they were doing it alone
Only 2 of 12 interviewees asked about offline use

do.text: Launch to one campus before spreading
do.why: Groups need friends on the app; density matters more than reach

do.text: Measure week-2 retention above everything else
do.why: Quitting in week 2 is the exact problem the product claims to solve

dont.why: Interviewees found leaderboards stressful; the product is about support, not ranking

dont.text: Don't build sync or a backend of your own
dont.why: That's what blew the first estimate up to 10 weeks

items.text: Campus licence sales cycles are long
items.mitigation: Start with a free campus pilot; don't depend on licence revenue in year one

items.text: Groups go quiet after the first week
items.mitigation: Daily group nudge when half the group has checked in; measure week-2 retention in the pilot

items.text: A solo developer becomes a bottleneck
items.mitigation: Keep the MVP to five features; no custom backend code beyond Supabase
